scope: Protocol state receipt-time retention across executor and protocol mutex waits; no native-owner reservation or production delegation handout

checks: default lease is 60 seconds; configured five-second lease is advertised and SEQUENCE renews OPEN beyond its initial expiry
SEQUENCE and exact replay on either session renew the shared client lease and keep an idle sibling session and its OPEN usable
idle session and OPEN expire at the advertised lease; another client opens the file while the expired stateid remains invalid
reducing the lease preserves the old reclaim window across repeated restarts, then converges to the configured duration after grace
complete TCP request reaches the bounded executor before lease expiry and retains OPEN beyond expiry while both workers are occupied
successful SEQUENCE renews after the delay; queued READ returns original data; suspended file worker was not replaced
one context shared across 32 sessions and three TCP paths admits only its 64-entry RPC window; completing the oldest request releases the next authenticated callback
krb5/krb5i/krb5p CB_NULL, CB_SEQUENCE and CB_NOTIFY_LOCK use real Kerberos, independent RPC counters and exact referring calls; notifications grant no lock
BACKCHANNEL_CTL rejects unknown handles/invalid services/oversized RPC credentials atomically; existing handles are idempotent and counters never reset
BACKCHANNEL_CTL adds handles instead of replacing them; empty additions retain GSS, and destruction of another context preserves the live path
sixteen live callback tuples are bounded; exhaustion preserves the existing channel and duplicate offers consume no extra capacity
negotiated channel sizes include exact GSS credential, MIC and wrapped-body overhead; exact request limits succeed and one-byte-short channels send no oversized callbacks
unsigned, bad MIC/ciphertext and wrong authenticated sequences cannot complete callbacks; disconnect/rebind retries exact CB_SEQUENCE plaintext with fresh RPC authentication
authenticated integrity/privacy DELAY replies retry unchanged slots on live transports; established slot faults report BACKCHANNEL_FAULT through the protected forechannel
nearly expired and expired contexts set SEQUENCE flags; expiry/destroy removes path authority without AUTH_NONE fallback, and fresh contexts restore it
AUTH_SYS and authentication-only Kerberos cannot establish SP4_SSV
empty algorithms, zero window, unsupported OIDs and forbidden hash/cipher combinations return protocol errors
